BEFORE YOU START

A few good
questions.

Read the setup guide
What exactly is Ultharness?

Ultharness is a local workspace for coding agents and client delivery. Capture a detailed brief, define acceptance criteria, let an agent build, run project checks, and review the result through a bounded repair cycle. You make the final acceptance decision.

Does it come with the AI models?

The Mac app includes its dashboard, local server, Node, npm, and npx. Codex, Claude, OmniRoute, Ollama, provider accounts, and local model weights are separate installations. Model availability, usage costs, and quotas depend on your configured providers.

Can it automatically build a client website?

It can run an approved build, check, review, and repair cycle using an installed coding agent. The result depends on your brief, model capability, project dependencies, tools, and meaningful verification. Missing access and failed requirements need attention; the app doesn’t guarantee a finished site from every prompt.

How does it know the work is ready?

Required files and configured npm scripts produce recorded evidence. A separate agent session assesses each acceptance criterion. Failed checks or a rejected review can trigger repairs within your selected limit. Work that passes waits for your own review and acceptance.

What can I connect?

Add reference links and project documents for designs, repositories, CMSs, databases, APIs, and hosting. Configured MCP connections provide selected read tools to the builder. Use OmniRoute for model routing. Saving a reference doesn’t authenticate to that service or enable production writes.

Which Macs does it support?

The current build is for Apple silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later. It is ad-hoc signed and isn’t Apple-notarized. Download the disk image, drag Ultharness into Applications, then configure your installed agents and connect a project folder.
